# Conviction data show a much smaller difference than suspect data (fixture)

> **FIXTURE — not a real source.** Written for the test suite. The numbers illustrate a structure; they are not evidence about the world.

Studies that use conviction records rather than arrest or suspect records find much
smaller differences between groups, and the differences that remain track socioeconomic
status and neighbourhood rather than origin. This is expected if suspect records are
sensitive to policing intensity and reporting behaviour while conviction records are not.
The measurement instrument, not only the population, determines the size of the observed
difference.
